turns.zh: 本集由 Eppo 为您带来。 Eppo 是 Airbnb 校友为现代增长团队打造的下一代 AB 测试平台。 Netlify、Contentful 和 Cameo 等公司依靠 Eppo 来支持他们的实验。无论您在哪里工作，进行实验都变得越来越重要，但没有可以与现代增长团队堆栈集成的商业工具。这会导致浪费时间构建内部工具或尝试通过笨重的营销工具进行实验。当我在 Airbnb 工作时，我喜欢我们的实验平台的一件事是能够轻松地按设备、国家和用户阶段划分结果。 (00:31:16)：Eppo 做到了这一切，甚至更多。快速提供结果，避免恼人的长时间分析周期，并帮助您轻松找到所发现问题的根本原因。 Eppo 让您超越基本的点击率指标，而是使用我们的北极星指标，例如激活、保留、订阅和付款。 Eppo支持前端、后端、电子邮件营销甚至机器学习客户端的测试。请访问 geteppo.com 查看 Eppo。 Geteppo.com 和 10 倍的实验速度。所以第一步，就是要弄清楚你是如何成长的。就 Gojek 而言，这部分是现实世界，人们只是看到 Gojek 骑着马到处走。

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: I think it's both figure out how you're growing and also the elements that you have at your disposal. What are the levers that you have that maybe you've never tried using? When we looked at our model this way, we actually realized we had underutilized the driver's capacity to drive our growth. Pun definitely intended. So in looking at the model this way, we had thought through what is our goal. We want GoPay to be much bigger than it really is. It's a E-wallet service, users are able to get access to this digital balance. How do we drive adoption? And so when we looked at the lever of we have a driver, we actually created an incentive model. So we built a very small service that would check when a driver got allocated to a customer, again, the product and the model, we would then check in the database, has this customer ever used our GoPay product before? (00:32:59): Did they have a digital balance? And if the answer was no, we would message the driver immediately, "Hey, this customer hasn't done a GoPay top up before. If you get them to give you cash and we deposit it into their virtual wallet, we'll give you extra money." So using them as the salesperson. You wouldn't believe how great of a salesperson someone can be when you were literally trapped in a car with them going somewhere. And so you have this captive audience, captive attention, you have someone who has the incentive to cross pay or cross sell someone into GoPay. And customers were able to feel the benefit because the driver was explaining it to them directly. There was no change to the physics, it was a lever usage.
turns.zh: 我认为这既要弄清楚你是如何成长的，也是你可以使用的元素。您拥有哪些可能从未尝试过使用的杠杆？当我们以这种方式审视我们的模型时，我们实际上意识到我们没有充分利用驾驶员的能力来推动我们的增长。双关语绝对是故意的。因此，在以这种方式看待模型时，我们思考了我们的目标是什么。我们希望 GoPay 的规模比实际规模大得多。这是一项电子钱包服务，用户可以访问该数字余额。我们如何推动采用？因此，当我们考虑拥有司机的杠杆时，我们实际上创建了一个激励模型。因此，我们建立了一个非常小的服务，可以检查司机何时分配给客户，以及产品和型号，然后我们会检查数据库，该客户以前是否使用过我们的 GoPay 产品？ (00:32:59)：他们有数字天平吗？如果答案是否定的，我们会立即给司机发消息，“嘿，这位顾客以前没有进行过 GoPay 充值。如果你让他们给你现金，我们将其存入他们的虚拟钱包，我们会给你额外的钱。”所以用他们作为销售人员。当你真的被困在车里和他们一起去某个地方时，你不会相信某人能成为多么出色的销售人员。因此，你拥有了这些被俘获的受众、被俘获的注意力，你有一个有动力交叉支付或交叉销售某人到 GoPay 的人。客户能够感受到好处，因为司机直接向他们解释。物理原理没有改变，只是杠杆的使用。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What a devious strategy.
turns.zh: 多么狡猾的策略啊。

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: It was huge. It was 60% of acquisition once we released that.
turns.zh: 它是巨大的。当我们发布该信息时，该数字已占收购量的 60%。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh my God. So for thinking through your potential levers and physics of your growth, do you think about it bottoms up, here's all the things that are going on and here's areas we can invest? Or do you have a menu of options top down of here's the 10 things it could be, it's looking like for Gojek it's these four and let's focus on that?
turns.zh: 我的天啊。因此，在思考你的潜在杠杆和增长物理过程时，你是否会自下而上地思考，这是正在发生的所有事情以及我们可以投资的领域？或者你有一个从上到下的选项菜单，其中可能有 10 件事，对于 Gojek 来说就是这四件事，让我们重点关注这一点？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. I think you always have to start from the fact that we are not wizards. It's very hard to move the physics of a universe when you are trying these new things. So start with what currently works and currently exists and where you think the biggest constraint is or the best lever is, and then fix that one piece because the entire universe isn't exploding. The world isn't changing so dramatically that your physics change. So I think rooted in reality is very important.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为你总是必须从我们不是巫师这一事实开始。当你尝试这些新事物时，很难改变宇宙的物理原理。因此，从当前有效和当前存在的内容以及您认为最大的限制或最佳杠杆所在开始，然后修复该部分，因为整个宇宙不会爆炸。世界并没有发生如此巨大的变化，以至于你的物理学发生了变化。所以我觉得植根于现实非常重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. Okay. So it's see what's working, find the constraints. And then step two is basically what can you do to the product to optimize the funnel/loop to make it go even faster?
turns.zh: 知道了。好的。所以要看看什么在起作用，找到限制。第二步基本上是你可以对产品做些什么来优化漏斗/循环，使其运行得更快？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 确切地。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Love that. Maybe as another example, if something comes to mind, with Kumu, how do you think of Kumu through this lens?
turns.zh: 喜欢那个。也许再举个例子，如果你想到 Kumu，你通过这个镜头如何看待 Kumu？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. I'm always very hesitant to talk about Kumu, because there's so much competition right now and we are on the cusp of some very interesting things. But I think for Kumu, it's actually very complex because there's a lot of human emotion that is involved. With Gojek you knew if you got the job done. You made a transaction. With Kumu, how do you know if a consumer made a friend, felt like they had a genuine friendship? So you almost have to create more friction to identify users who really got past that barrier and aren't explicit with the activity that they did. So we have features that tell us if a user is really searching for this job to be done, if they really want to be part of a community, how do they fill out this? (00:35:57): Do they fill out the form? Do they fill out a questionnaire of many questions? Do they go through this friction just to get access to a community? So we almost create this artificial friction to help differentiate how deeply a user wants something or needs something. And if the user doesn't fill out that questionnaire, maybe they're actually looking for something else. They were looking for entertainment. They were looking for content or short form content. And so creating almost like hand razor approaches for a user to say, "I wanted this thing." We leave a lot of breadcrumbs in the app to be able to identify those paths.
turns.zh: 是的。我总是很犹豫是否要谈论 Kumu，因为现在竞争非常激烈，而且我们正处于一些非常有趣的事情的风口浪尖。但我认为对于 Kumu 来说，它实际上非常复杂，因为涉及到很多人类情感。有了 Gojek，您就知道自己是否完成了工作。你做了一笔交易。有了 Kumu，你怎么知道消费者是否交了朋友，是否感觉他们有真正的友谊？因此，您几乎必须制造更多摩擦来识别真正克服了这一障碍并且对他们所做的活动不明确的用户。因此，我们有一些功能可以告诉我们用户是否真的在寻找要完成的工作，如果他们真的想成为社区的一部分，他们如何填写这个？ (00:35:57)：他们填写表格吗？他们是否填写了包含许多问题的调查问卷？他们经历这种摩擦只是为了进入社区吗？因此，我们几乎创造了这种人为的摩擦，以帮助区分用户想要某物或需要某物的深度。如果用户没有填写该调查问卷，也许他们实际上是在寻找其他东西。他们正在寻找娱乐。他们正在寻找内容或简短的内容。因此，创建几乎类似于手动剃须刀的方法，让用户说：“我想要这个东西。”我们在应用程序中留下了很多面包屑，以便能够识别这些路径。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. While we're on the topic of these two companies, just maybe for inspiration to founders who are thinking of ways to drive growth, what were a couple of the bigger unlocks growth wise for these two companies or even any other company that you've worked with that's interesting?
turns.zh: 惊人的。当我们讨论这两家公司的话题时，也许只是为了给那些正在思考如何推动增长的创始人带来启发，那么对于这两家公司甚至您合作过的任何其他公司来说，有哪些更大的增长智慧？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. Definitely, in the early days it was copy. So I think if your product does something that's not super familiar, you have to tie it to something that is. So I talked about using drivers to sell GoPay. Before that, one thing that we did was to actually take someone's virtual account number and put it onto a picture of a credit card. You know what a credit card is, that's familiar to you. A lot of people didn't know what a digital wallet was. And so when they looked at this like, "Oh, okay. I have this virtual thing that acts like a credit card. It works like my debit account." Then they understood the concept a lot better. (00:37:33): And we actually saw top ups increase based on us, literally just sending that picture with someone's virtual account number there. So they could go to an ATM and they would just type in the card number as they would a regular debit account. And they realized that they could top up through that channel. Because that was something that was pretty interesting to us, with just how do we tie the familiarity loop back into the consumer mental model of the product and drive acquisition that way?
turns.zh: 是的。当然，在早期它是复制的。所以我认为，如果你的产品做了一些不太熟悉的事情，你就必须将它与熟悉的东西联系起来。所以我就谈到了利用司机来销售GoPay。在此之前，我们所做的一件事就是实际获取某人的虚拟帐号并将其放在信用卡的图片上。您知道什么是信用卡，这对您来说很熟悉。很多人不知道什么是数字钱包。所以当他们看到这个的时候，“哦，好吧。我有这个虚拟的东西，它的作用就像信用卡。它就像我的借记账户一样。”然后他们对这个概念有了更好的理解。 (00:37:33)：我们实际上看到充值量随着我们的增加而增加，实际上只是将带有某人虚拟帐号的图片发送到那里。因此，他们可以去 ATM 机，只需输入卡号，就像输入常规借记账户一样。他们意识到他们可以通过该渠道充值。因为这对我们来说非常有趣，我们如何将熟悉度循环与产品的消费者心智模型联系起来并以这种方式推动购买？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And that was at Gojek?
turns.zh: 那是在Gojek？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything else maybe, since you don't want to talk too much about Kumu, any other advisorships or companies, examples of something that ended up working really well to help them accelerate growth?
turns.zh: 既然您不想过多谈论 Kumu、任何其他咨询公司或公司，还有其他什么东西最终能很好地帮助他们加速增长的例子吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Things that have worked really well. So for one of the companies I work with, AB&B, they run a lot of their D2C brands in South America and globally. So one of the features that we were looking at was how do we ensure that subscriptions don't actually become a canceling point for a user. So in the app you could cancel or you could resume your subscription, but you couldn't pause it. So when we looked at the cancellation reasons and we saw that their number one reason was, I still have too much fear, we actually decided, well, let's just add a pause button then. (00:38:58): Because canceling the subscription is a permanent solution to having too much fear. How do you make a temporary solution that solves the actual problem? Adding in a pause button actually helped alleviate a lot of the churn that was becoming very hard to reacquire back. So that was one fix where we looked at the, again, physics of the model. We're not going to create new changes to the product or create one time buys or reactivation emails. We'll just solve the problem at that small constraint where everyone drops off.
turns.zh: 效果非常好的事情。因此，对于我合作的公司之一 AB&B，他们在南美和全球运营着许多 D2C 品牌。因此，我们正在研究的功能之一是如何确保订阅实际上不会成为用户的取消点。因此，在应用程序中，您可以取消或恢复订阅，但无法暂停。因此，当我们查看取消原因时，我们发现他们的首要原因是，我仍然有太多的恐惧，我们实际上决定，好吧，让我们添加一个暂停按钮。 (00:38:58)：因为取消订阅是解决过度恐惧的永久解决方案。如何制定临时解决方案来解决实际问题？添加暂停按钮实际上有助于减轻很多很难重新恢复的流失。因此，这是我们再次研究模型物理原理的一个解决方案。我们不会对产品进行新的更改，也不会创建一次性购买或重新激活电子邮件。我们将在每个人都退出的小约束下解决问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wait, so can you order beer as subscription? Is that a thing? Is this a consumer product or is this-
turns.zh: 等等，你可以订阅啤酒吗？这是一件事吗？这是消费品还是——

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: It was a thing, yeah.
turns.zh: 这是一件事，是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool. Okay. This also reminds me, at Airbnb, this was actually one of the biggest wins, is adding a snooze feature to your listing. Exactly the same thing. Yeah. All right there we go. Awesome. Tip for folks that have churn problems, snooze/pause. I want to shift a little bit to a post that you wrote that maybe is one of your more popular posts you wrote on the Reforge blog called Why Most Analytics Efforts Fail. And I'd love to hear your broad overview of why do most analytics efforts fail and then how do teams avoid this? Maybe what are two to three things they can do?
turns.zh: 凉爽的。好的。这也提醒我，在 Airbnb，这实际上是最大的胜利之一，就是在您的房源中添加小睡功能。完全一样的事情。是的。好吧，我们走吧。惊人的。对于有流失问题的人来说，建议暂停/暂停。我想稍微转移一下您写的一篇文章，这可能是您在 Reforge 博客上写的最受欢迎的文章之一，名为“为什么大多数分析工作都会失败”。我很想听听您对为什么大多数分析工作失败以及团队如何避免这种情况的广泛概述？也许他们能做的两到三件事是什么？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah, I'm actually pretty surprised at how much noise that has generated because I guess it came from a place of frustration where I kept telling people like, "You are doing this wrong. Here's how you should probably be doing it." But I think it resonated a lot with folks because they recognize all of those symptoms, but they weren't sure why it was happening. So to say, oh, this is the thing, instrumentation is what's wrong, I think it's a very actionable thing. It's probably one of the most solvable problems out there. It just takes some time and mental model shifts to do it well. So a lot of people look at tracking data as how do I track my OKR? How do I know if I'm going up or down? But they don't use it to track or identify insights. So I will use the example of using Twitter for "news" when in reality they're actually using Twitter for entertainment. (00:41:17): Do not treat metric gathering as entertainment. It's not there for you to be like, "Oh, that's interesting, how novel," and then not act on it. So real news is information that changes what you do in the real world. And if you don't change what you're doing, what you are doing is just getting entertainment. So let's use that as the premise. The next step in instrumentation is to look at the fact that measurements do not equate to insights. A measurement would be an observation. It's a data point in your database. So the example being power users do four times more bookings, is an all observed fact because your transactional database obviously says that is the case, but it's on an insight because it doesn't have context. It doesn't give you information that lets you act on it and better understand the problem. (00:42:11): So another example would be if I see my girlfriend hanging out with a guy I don't know, that is an observed fact that you see in the real world. Your hypothesis could be that your girlfriend is cheating on you, but the insight, the actual fact might be that she's not cheating on you, it's her cousin. And now your insight is, I am paranoid and I need to change my behavior to be less crazy. So the insight will provide value when you have this, why answered? Why is this person doing this thing? Here's why. And then you are going to act differently. So for our purposes, if we look at a GoFood user will transact and is more likely to use a voucher, that's a fact, that's an observation, but it's not an insight. An insight would be something like GoFood users who are power users are more likely to use a free shipping discount on a high GMV basket versus non-power users. (00:43:22): And that actually tells you how to change your marketing approach. It tells you in what circumstances does someone do this. When it's a high GMV basket, give power users the ability to get a free discount, but do not do this for non-powered users because they won't convert any better than they normally would. So, that helps you change your marketing spend. It helps you understand the decision points of power users versus non-power users. The insight is instrumenting properties into an event so that you can segment who is doing what behavior and make some hypotheses on that observation. Test that hypothesis, and then you get some causal representation of whether or not that hypothesis was right.
turns.zh: 是的，我实际上对产生的噪音感到非常惊讶，因为我猜它来自于一个沮丧的地方，我一直告诉人们，“你做错了。这就是你应该如何做的。”但我认为它引起了人们的强烈共鸣，因为他们认识到所有这些症状，但他们不确定为什么会发生。所以说，哦，这就是问题，仪器仪表就是出了问题，我认为这是一个非常可行的事情。这可能是最容易解决的问题之一。只需要一些时间和思维模式的转变就能做好。因此，很多人将跟踪数据视为如何跟踪我的 OKR？我怎么知道我是上升还是下降？但他们不会用它来跟踪或识别见解。因此，我将使用使用 Twitter 来获取“新闻”的示例，而实际上他们使用 Twitter 是为了娱乐。 (00:41:17)：不要将度量收集视为娱乐。你不会说，“哦，这很有趣，多么新颖”，然后就不采取行动。所以真正的新闻是改变你在现实世界中所做的事情的信息。如果你不改变你正在做的事情，你所做的只是为了娱乐。那么我们以此为前提。仪器仪表化的下一步是审视测量并不等于洞察这一事实。测量就是观察。它是数据库中的一个数据点。因此，高级用户的预订量增加四倍的例子是一个所有观察到的事实，因为您的事务数据库显然表明情况如此，但它是基于洞察力，因为它没有上下文。它不会提供让您采取行动并更好地理解问题的信息。 (00:42:11)：另一个例子是，如果我看到我的女朋友和一个我不认识的人出去玩，这是你在现实世界中看到的一个观察到的事实。你的假设可能是你的女朋友在欺骗你，但洞察力，实际的事实可能是她没有欺骗你，而是她的表弟。现在你的见解是，我很偏执，我需要改变我的行为，让自己不那么疯狂。因此，当你有了这个见解时，洞察力就会提供价值，为什么要回答呢？这个人为什么要做这件事？原因如下。然后你就会采取不同的行动。因此，就我们的目的而言，如果我们观察 GoFood 用户是否会进行交易并且更有可能使用优惠券，这是事实，这是一种观察，但不是洞察。一种见解是，与非高级用户相比，高级用户 GoFood 用户更有可能在高 GMV 购物篮中使用免费送货折扣。 (00:43:22)：这实际上告诉您如何改变营销方式。它告诉您某人在什么情况下会这样做。当 GMV 较高时，让高级用户能够获得免费折扣，但不要对非高级用户这样做，因为他们不会比平常更好地进行转化。因此，这可以帮助您改变营销支出。它可以帮助您了解高级用户与非高级用户的决策点。洞察力是将属性插入到事件中，以便您可以细分谁在做什么行为，并根据观察结果做出一些假设。检验该假设，然后您就可以得到该假设是否正确的一些因果表示。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So it sounds like a lot of the root of the issue is setting up the wrong metrics, the wrong... I guess there's the tracking element of just capturing the right information. And then also just not focusing on insights versus just having a bunch of information.
turns.zh: 因此，听起来很多问题的根源在于设置了错误的指标，错误的……我想存在只是捕获正确信息的跟踪元素。然后，也不关注洞察力，而只关注大量信息。

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 确切地。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What are signs that you're doing this? Say someone's going to go load up their dashboard and they're like, "Am I failing or not?" What should they be looking for?
turns.zh: 有哪些迹象表明您正在这样做？假设有人要加载他们的仪表板，他们会想，“我是否失败了？”他们应该寻找什么？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: So I already know if a team is good at instrumentation or not just by looking at the instrumentation spec. The symptom of a bad data tracking approach is you have a ton of rows with a ton of events, but every event has one property or no property being tracked. So an example with Gojek would be when a user lands on the map to select a drop off point, the event would be drop off or map loaded, let's say. And the properties there should be things like how many drivers do they see on the screen? What is the pickup location? What city is it in? What latitude and longitude is it? Is there surge pricing? What is the current minimum fare? Do they have a voucher code? (00:45:28): All of these characteristics of the experience and the context that can help you look at hey, when a user only sees two drivers on the screen, they're much less likely to convert than a user who sees five drivers on a screen. Now we can look at in what cities and in what latitude and longitudes do we mostly only see two drivers versus five drivers. Being able to do the second layer approach of the why and not just stop at, "That's weird. When you have two drivers you are less likely to book." But then you never ask why. That drives me crazy. Or the inability to even know that there were only two drivers on the screen. You're missing so much context of the user's experience that you're unable to make assumptions about why the user didn't convert.
turns.zh: 因此，我已经知道一个团队是否擅长仪器仪表，而不仅仅是通过查看仪表规格。糟糕的数据跟踪方法的症状是，您有大量包含大量事件的行，但每个事件都有一个属性或没有属性被跟踪。因此，Gojek 的一个例子是，当用户登陆地图选择下车点时，事件将被下车或地图加载。那里的属性应该是诸如他们在屏幕上看到多少个驱动程序之类的东西？上车地点是什么？它在哪个城市？它的纬度和经度是多少？有峰时定价吗？目前的最低票价是多少？他们有优惠券代码吗？ (00:45:28)：体验和上下文的所有这些特征可以帮助您了解，嘿，当用户在屏幕上只看到两个驱动程序时，他们比在屏幕上看到五个驱动程序的用户转换的可能性要小得多。现在我们可以看看在哪些城市以及哪些纬度和经度，我们大多只看到两名司机而不是五名司机。能够采用第二层方法来了解原因，而不仅仅是停留在“这很奇怪。当你有两个司机时，你预订的可能性就较小。”但你永远不会问为什么。这让我发疯。或者甚至无法知道屏幕上只有两个驱动程序。您缺少太多有关用户体验的背景信息，以至于您无法假设用户没有进行转化的原因。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this. Maybe your course is probably going to be the answer, but for folks that want to figure out how to do this taxonomy and events well, how do they go about doing that?
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个。也许你的课程可能就是答案，但是对于那些想要弄清楚如何做好这种分类和事件的人来说，他们该如何去做呢？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: So I think it's important to just go through examples. Yes, every product is different, but everyone has the same signup flow for the most part. So look at the signup flow examples that I have in the blog post or in, I believe Amplitude actually has a pretty good long-winded documentation on this, on how to do a event tracking. But it's really a matter of sitting down and thinking really deeply. If I were to press this button, why would I and why would I not? And am I tracking that in my user properties? So it's really just sitting down and mapping out the experience.
turns.zh: 所以我认为仅通过示例很重要。是的，每种产品都是不同的，但大多数情况下每个人都有相同的注册流程。因此，看看我在博客文章或中的注册流程示例，我相信 Amplitude 实际上有一个关于如何进行事件跟踪的非常好的冗长文档。但这确实是一个坐下来认真思考的问题。如果我按下这个按钮，我为什么会按下，为什么不按下？我是否在我的用户属性中跟踪它？所以实际上只是坐下来规划体验。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Speaking of Amplitude and other data tools, do you have a default recommended metrics stack for our founders just to start with and maybe a few other things as they evolve?
turns.zh: 说到 Amplitude 和其他数据工具，您是否有一个默认的推荐指标堆栈供我们的创始人开始使用，也许随着他们的发展还有其他一些东西？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: That really depends on how early they are. So if they have a single data warehouse with all of their transactional data, usually I say, you can probably get by with Google Data Studio. It's free usually with whatever you're using. If not Metabase has a great open source free tool. If you have someone who can write SQL or if you have multiple databases, then Metabase is great. If you need in app mobile device event tracking, I usually recommend CleverTap because Mixpanel has unfortunately failed me a lot. And Amplitude doesn't have the CRM components that I would need all in one space. (00:47:51): If I am much bigger and I need more analytics juice, maybe Amplitude makes sense on top of this, or something that helps me pipe data into more dashboards and do less ETL for me. Then I would get into Segment. And then once you get into experimentation, obviously I have to shout out to Eppo. I think they've really instrumented a lot of the dashboards that I would've normally had to do in experimentation projects. So I usually look at something like Eppo to just automate the decision making flow.
turns.zh: 这实际上取决于他们的早到程度。因此，如果他们有一个包含所有交易数据的数据仓库，通常我会说，你可能可以使用 Google Data Studio。无论您使用什么，它通常都是免费的。如果没有的话，Metabase 有一个很棒的开源免费工具。如果您有人会编写 SQL 或者您有多个数据库，那么 Metabase 就很棒。如果您需要在应用程序中跟踪移动设备事件，我通常推荐 CleverTap，因为 Mixpanel 不幸地让我失望了很多。而且 Amplitude 没有将我需要的所有 CRM 组件集中在一个空间中。 (00:47:51)：如果我规模更大并且需要更多分析能力，也许 Amplitude 更有意义，或者可以帮助我将数据传输到更多仪表板并为我执行更少的 ETL。然后我会进入细分市场。一旦你开始实验，显然我必须向 Eppo 大声喊叫。我认为他们确实对我通常在实验项目中必须做的很多仪表板进行了检测。因此，我通常会使用 Eppo 之类的工具来自动化决策流程。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. I think we're both small investors in Eppo, big fans, a little bit of bias, but yeah's it's an excellent Airbnb team that built it, so it's cool. Shifting a bit from metrics and data to just growth teams in general, maybe first question is just, how do you recommend companies set up a growth team in the early days and then over time?
turns.zh: 惊人的。我认为我们都是 Eppo 的小投资者，大粉丝，有点偏见，但是是的，这是一个优秀的 Airbnb 团队建造的，所以它很酷。从指标和数据转向一般的增长团队，也许第一个问题只是，您如何建议公司在早期建立增长团队，然后随着时间的推移？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. So I can talk about how growth was set up at Gojek as an example, which I think is probably the best practice. So we didn't really know what growth was at that time, but we knew there were obvious gaps to fill. So because we had grown so quickly, the core product team was still making the core product features. As simple as phone number masking. That wasn't a thing yet. You had access to your driver's phone number. It's probably not a great thing. It's probably part of the core functionality and we need to fill that gap. At the same time, growth was still necessary because you had all of these users trying to use a product that aren't quite getting there. (00:49:25): So things like figuring out what SMS provider we should use to send the OTP to this user who is signing up from this telco provider. That was a growth objective that isn't necessarily core feature work, but was a gap to fill given the onboarding and SMS success delivery rates. Things like telling the driver if this was a brand new customer, because at this point in time, drivers had taken thousands of rides and they assumed every single customer knew how Gojek worked, when maybe they didn't. And so we knew that the protocol was that a power user would know they would make an order and they would just wait. They would wait somewhere, they would keep an eye out for a driver and then they would get on the motorcycle and go. (00:50:13): But for a brand new user, are you supposed to walk to the driver? Are you supposed to find them? It's unclear to this brand new, uneducated new user how to use the product. And so first time user experience could have been a terrible one where they went and walked off and then the driver came to the pickup point and they couldn't find them. So it was all of these small acquisition, adoption and engagement use cases that growth was filling the gap on. And eventually we embedded our growth, I would say product managers at the time, into these teams and they ended up synthesizing what growth was as a full-time role. Eventually becoming PMs who own specific parts of the product stack.
turns.zh: 是的。所以我可以以 Gojek 为例来谈谈增长是如何建立的，我认为这可能是最佳实践。所以当时我们并不真正知道增长是什么，但我们知道有明显的空白需要填补。因此，由于我们发展得如此之快，核心产品团队仍在开发核心产品功能。就像电话号码屏蔽一样简单。那还不是事。您可以访问司机的电话号码。这或许不是什么好事。它可能是核心功能的一部分，我们需要填补这个空白。与此同时，增长仍然是必要的，因为所有这些用户都在尝试使用尚未完全实现目标的产品。 (00:49:25)：比如弄清楚我们应该使用哪个 SMS 提供商将 OTP 发送给从该电信提供商注册的用户。这是一个增长目标，不一定是核心功能工作，但考虑到入职和短信成功发送率，这是一个需要填补的空白。比如告诉司机这是否是一个全新的客户，因为在这个时候，司机已经乘坐了数千次车，他们假设每个客户都知道 Gojek 是如何工作的，而实际上他们可能并不知道。所以我们知道协议是高级用户知道他们会下订单并且他们只会等待。他们会在某个地方等待，留意司机，然后骑上摩托车出发。 (00:50:13)：但是对于一个全新的用户来说，你应该走到司机那里吗？你应该找到他们吗？对于这个全新的、未受过教育的新用户来说，不清楚如何使用该产品。因此，第一次用户体验可能会很糟糕，他们走开，然后司机来到接送点，但他们找不到他们。因此，正是所有这些小型收购、采用和参与用例，增长才填补了空白。最终，我们将我们的增长（我想说当时的产品经理）融入到这些团队中，他们最终将增长作为一个全职角色进行了综合。最终成为拥有产品堆栈特定部分的产品经理。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So in your experience, and I hear this a lot, is your first growth person shouldn't just come in and figure out what to work on. You should understand here's where we need growth help, let's find somebody to tackle it, versus come help us figure out what to do to drive growth. Is that how you've seen it?
turns.zh: 因此，根据你的经验，我经常听到这样的话，你的第一个成长型人员不应该只是进来弄清楚要做什么。你应该明白，这就是我们需要增长帮助的地方，让我们找人来解决这个问题，而不是来帮助我们弄清楚如何推动增长。你是这样看的吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Exactly. I think it's just setting the bar too high to expect someone to come in and model everything. Again, there are physics in place it's very hard to move everything. So it's really about having someone who already has all of this data knows where the biggest gaps are. Doesn't have to start from scratch and figure this out and then just picks some small space to work on that they know is workable.
turns.zh: 确切地。我认为这只是把标准设置得太高了，以至于不能指望有人进来并对一切进行建模。再说一遍，有物理原理，很难移动所有东西。因此，真正重要的是让已经拥有所有这些数据的人知道最大的差距在哪里。不必从头开始解决这个问题，然后只选择一些他们知道可行的小空间来工作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have strong opinions about growth being integrated? The way that you described where growth PM basically has a cross functional team basically is the PM versus a separate growth team that's off to the side.
turns.zh: 您对整合增长有强烈的看法吗？您所描述的增长 PM 基本上拥有一个跨职能团队的方式基本上是 PM 与偏向一边的独立增长团队。

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. I think it can work as a separate growth team to the side if the company is truly head over heels, tripping on insane product market fit, if there's insane, product market fit and you are really scrambling to do core feature stacks, then maybe a growth team to come and be clean up is fine. We're the cleanup crew. We pick up the pieces that were left behind, we connect the dots. You forgot to plug this in, we'll plug it in for you. But we were a team of lots of stats heavy people. So a lot of my team were statistics graduates. We cared a lot about looking at numbers and odds and probabilities because it really is a numbers game at that scale. You could work on anything and everything would probably do something. But what was the thing that would make the most impact now and unlock us for the future.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为，如果公司真的神魂颠倒，被疯狂的产品市场契合所绊倒，那么它可以作为一个独立的增长团队在一边工作，如果有疯狂的产品市场契合，而你真的在争先恐后地做核心功能堆栈，那么也许一个增长团队来清理就可以了。我们是清洁工。我们拾起留下的碎片，将这些点连接起来。您忘记插入此插头，我们会为您插入。但我们是一支由很多注重数据的人组成的团队。所以我的团队中有很多人都是统计学毕业生。我们非常关心数字、赔率和概率，因为这确实是一个如此规模的数字游戏。你可以做任何事，而且每件事都可能有所作为。但什么是对现在产生最大影响并为我们开启未来的东西呢？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I was going to ask you folks to look for when they're hiring an early growth person, is that what you find, just stats, data kind of person?
turns.zh: 我想问你们，当他们招聘早期成长型人才时，你们会寻找这样的人吗？只是统计、数据类型的人吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: You have to have someone who knows how to run the numbers. If you're looking at ratios of conversion rates, but you don't realize that this ratio is of a much smaller base size, you're going to make the wrong decision. So someone who is intuitively good at statistics, they know how to do sampling appropriately. They know what selection bias is. The worst possible thing is to have a growth person who thinks they are doing the right thing and is measuring things wrong and then focusing on the wrong areas.
turns.zh: 你必须有一个知道如何计算数字的人。如果您正在查看转化率比率，但您没有意识到该比率的基础规模要小得多，那么您将做出错误的决定。因此，直觉上擅长统计的人，他们知道如何适当地进行抽样。他们知道什么是选择偏差。最糟糕的事情是，成长型人才认为自己正在做正确的事情，但却错误地衡量了事情，然后将注意力集中在错误的领域。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you find that it's often easier or better to hire a young up and coming person or find someone that's got a bunch of experience for your first growth hire?
turns.zh: 您是否发现雇用一位年轻有为的人才或找到一位经验丰富的人来为您的第一次成长招聘通常更容易或更好？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: I would hire someone who is willing to take intro to statistics course. And it doesn't matter if they've had the experience to go wild or not. I think it really is, can they focus on the right opportunity rather than the most flashy thing? And I think both profiles can come under that.
turns.zh: 我会聘请愿意参加统计课程入门的人。他们是否有过疯狂的经历并不重要。我想确实如此，他们能否专注于正确的机会而不是最华而不实的事情？我认为这两种情况都可以归入这一范畴。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. And then what do you do in a hiring process for someone like this? What kind of things do you suggest founders look for?
turns.zh: 知道了。那么在招聘过程中你会为这样的人做什么呢？您建议创始人寻找什么样的东西？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. I actually look for that first principle bias. So I'll give people case studies of here's what we see, how do you know that this is true? And then I have them set up an experiment design. I want to see that they are sampling randomly. Not that they're like, "I'm going to build this feature and launch it, and of course it's going to work." I want to see that they're taking a measured deliberate approach to considering why someone might do this or what tools are available. A growth team can go terribly wrong when they just try to onboard a bunch of brand new tools that don't integrate well and it takes six months to integrate fully, and then they get nothing done for six months. Everything in growth is an opportunity cost of time, trade off with what you could have been doing to the product in that time. (00:54:50): So we biased towards really quick hacky things. Like in the early days of Gojek growth, I think our first real growth experiment, we were actually still the data team at this time, was to connect a quick Python script to the Twilio API that we had access to. And we SMSd a bunch of drivers through a CSV that we uploaded that said like, "Hey, your acceptance rate is really low. You're not supposed to do that. Please accept all the rides that you are getting." And that actually increased acceptance rates by 2% across the board. And when we looked deeper into that data, it did even more so for brand new drivers. And so we then worked with the data driver onboarding team so that they could better facilitate the onboarding experience for their drivers.
turns.zh: 是的。我实际上在寻找第一原则偏见。因此，我将向人们提供我们所看到的案例研究，你怎么知道这是真的？然后我让他们设置了一个实验设计。我想看到他们是随机抽样的。他们并不是说，“我要构建这个功能并推出它，它当然会起作用。”我希望看到他们采取审慎的方法来考虑为什么有人会这样做或者有哪些工具可用。当增长团队只是尝试使用一堆无法很好集成的全新工具并且需要六个月才能完全集成，然后他们在六个月内什么也没做时，他们可能会犯下严重错误。增长中的一切都是时间的机会成本，权衡你当时可以对产品做的事情。 (00:54:50)：所以我们偏向于真正快速的黑客事物。就像 Gojek 发展的早期一样，我认为我们的第一个真正的增长实验（当时我们实际上仍然是数据团队）是将一个快速的 Python 脚本连接到我们可以访问的 Twilio API。我们通过上传的 CSV 向一群司机发送短信，内容如下：“嘿，你们的接受率真的很低。你们不应该这样做。请接受你们收到的所有行程。”这实际上使整体录取率提高了 2%。当我们更深入地研究这些数据时，对于全新的驾驶员来说更是如此。因此，我们随后与数据驾驶员入职团队合作，以便他们能够更好地促进驾驶员的入职体验。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For the interview question that you described, an experiment design question, do you give that as a project where they have time to work on it or is it a live thing?
turns.zh: 对于你所描述的面试问题，一个实验设计问题，你是否将其作为一个项目，让他们有时间进行研究，或者它是一个活生生的事情吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yes. Yeah. I don't think live works really well for these case studies. I want to see people put in the time and the work to do something to the best of their ability. And of course we ask them like, "Hey, you have five days. We expect you to spend probably four hours on this, so if you don't have four hours within these five days, let us know." So we're pretty careful about giving them the appropriate amount of time to do it at the level of quality that we would've expected if they were to work here full-time. So give them those four hours, we want to see do they Google. If they can't figure it out right now, let's see them Google it. We'll ask them what approaches they took, how did they figure this out. And we like to hear people say that they literally had to Google this and read a bunch of white papers. I do that as well.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。我认为现场直播对于这些案例研究来说效果并不好。我希望看到人们投入时间和工作，尽其所能地做一些事情。当然，我们会问他们，“嘿，你有五天时间。我们预计你可能会花四个小时来做​​这件事，所以如果你在这五天内没有四个小时，请告诉我们。”因此，我们非常谨慎地给予他们适当的时间，以达到我们在他们全职工作时所期望的质量水平。所以给他们这四个小时，我们想看看他们是否谷歌。如果他们现在无法弄清楚，让我们看看他们用谷歌搜索一下。我们会问他们采取了什么方法，他们是如何解决这个问题的。我们喜欢听到人们说他们确实必须用谷歌搜索并阅读一堆白皮书。我也这样做。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For people trying to design one of these for themselves, do you have a question that you've retired that you could share or something that would help somebody design their own prompt?
turns.zh: 对于试图为自己设计其中一个提示的人来说，您是否有一个已经退休的问题可以分享，或者有什么可以帮助别人设计自己的提示的东西？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yeah. I can give you a template after this call.
turns.zh: 是的。这次通话后我可以给你一个模板。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. We'll include that in the show notes. Easy peasy. Amazing. Okay. A last topic that I wanted to cover is a very cool thing that you were involved in. It's a nonprofit that you started called Generation Girl. And I think the mission is to help women and young girls get into STEM. So I'd love to hear about this program, how you got into it, what it's all about, and then also just how listeners can help support what you're doing.
turns.zh: 惊人的。我们会将其包含在演出笔记中。简单易行。惊人的。好的。我想讲的最后一个主题是您参与的一件非常酷的事情。这是您创办的一个名为“Generation Girl”的非营利组织。我认为我们的使命是帮助女性和年轻女孩进入 STEM。所以我很想听听这个计划，你是如何参与这个计划的，它是关于什么的，以及听众如何帮助支持你正在做的事情。

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Absolutely. Yes. Generation Girl is very near and dear to my heart. So I co-founded this with a couple of amazing women who were also at Gojek, but are now full-time at Generation Girl. So this really stemmed from us repeatedly getting annoying comments about working in STEM. So things like, "You can't possibly be the engineer on this project. You look like you like makeup and stuff." And we were like, "Yes, I absolutely love makeup, but I also am badass at writing SWIFT code, so step aside." So having experienced a lot of the misrepresentation of what an engineer should look like or should like, I think we really look to Legally Blonde, is one of my favorite movies that represents you can take the powers that you have, whether you like engineering or design or data, and you can be whoever you want and still kick ass at it. (00:58:14): So a lot of the women that we support, we're actually happy if they go into one of our classes and they say, "Actually, I don't like engineering." That's great. That's agency and empowerment that they got to make that decision for themselves without any cultural biases or social pressure telling them that they should feel this way. And so we offer free classes for girls 12 to 17. We have college classes. We partner with teachers about how to teach STEM topics, especially in areas where they don't have laptops for every student. How do you teach how to use Figma and things like that? So people can definitely support us and reach out to us. We have a PayPal on our website, take a look.
turns.zh: 绝对地。是的。 《一代女孩》对我来说非常亲近。因此，我与几位出色的女性共同创立了这个公司，她们也曾在 Gojek，但现在全职在 Generation Girl。所以这实际上是因为我们不断收到关于 STEM 工作的恼人评论。比如，“你不可能是这个项目的工程师。你看起来喜欢化妆之类的东西。”我们的反应是，“是的，我非常喜欢化妆，但我也很擅长编写 SWIFT 代码，所以靠边站吧。”因此，在经历了很多关于工程师应该是什么样子或应该喜欢什么的误传之后，我认为我们真的很喜欢《律政俏佳人》，这是我最喜欢的电影之一，它代表着你可以掌握你所拥有的权力，无论你喜欢工程、设计还是数据，你可以成为任何你想要的人，并且仍然可以尽情发挥。 (00:58:14)：对于我们支持的很多女性来说，如果她们进入我们的一门课程并且说：“实际上，我不喜欢工程学”，我们实际上会很高兴。那太棒了。这是代理和授权，他们必须自己做出决定，没有任何文化偏见或社会压力告诉他们应该有这种感觉。因此，我们为 12 至 17 岁的女孩提供免费课程。我们有大学课程。我们与教师合作，探讨如何教授 STEM 主题，特别是在他们没有为每个学生配备笔记本电脑的领域。你是如何教授如何使用 Figma 之类的东西的？所以人们绝对可以支持我们并与我们联系。我们的网站上有 PayPal，您可以看看。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Can you share some of the impact that you've seen from this? Are there numbers you can share or anything that you can share around what the organizations have done.
turns.zh: 您能分享一下您从中看到的一些影响吗？您是否可以分享有关组织所做工作的数字或任何内容？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: So we've already had several thousand students go through Generation Girl, summer clubs and programs and classes. So we have an event every week. We have a full summer club that's every single day for two weeks, every summer and every winter. We have partnerships with some of the biggest tech companies in Indonesia, where we partner students with engineers and they work on projects together. And most recently we're part of the MIT solve program with our new initiative Class. So Class, we're creating a free to use site for teachers. (00:59:40): So right now we have partnered with a handful of universities in Indonesia, both in rural and city of Jakarta where teachers can now have the knowledge and material to explain newer concepts that maybe they're less familiar with, because startup world changes rapidly, how you develop changes rapidly. So this is one thing that we are most excited about because every teacher impacts thousands of students a year. And being able to teach the teachers and give them the resources that they need is something that's really important.
turns.zh: 因此，我们已经有数千名学生参加了“Generation Girl”、夏季俱乐部、项目和课程。所以我们每周都会举办一次活动。我们有一个完整的夏季俱乐部，每年夏天和每年冬天，两周内每天都举行。我们与印度尼西亚一些最大的科技公司建立了合作伙伴关系，我们将学生与工程师合作，他们一起开发项目。最近，我们通过新的倡议类参与了麻省理工学院解决方案项目。所以，班级，我们正在为教师创建一个免费使用的网站。 (00:59:40)：所以现在我们已经与印度尼西亚的几所大学合作，无论是在雅加达的农村还是城市，教师现在可以拥有知识和材料来解释他们可能不太熟悉的新概念，因为创业世界瞬息万变，你的发展方式也迅速变化。所以这是我们最兴奋的一件事，因为每位老师每年都会影响成千上万的学生。能够教授教师并为他们提供所需的资源是非常重要的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's incredible. It's currently just in Southeast Asia, is that right?
turns.zh: 那真是难以置信。目前仅在东南亚，对吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Only in Indonesia, because frankly, this is where everyone needs the most support. Globally STEM is not well received or welcoming at all to women. I think it's gotten worse over the past few decades. Below 18% of college graduates are women in computer science. So we're really trying to reach the youngest generation because that's when you are told or informed that computer science is for specific types of people.
turns.zh: Only in Indonesia, because frankly, this is where everyone needs the most support. Globally STEM is not well received or welcoming at all to women. I think it's gotten worse over the past few decades. Below 18% of college graduates are women in computer science.因此，我们确实在努力接触最年轻的一代，因为那时您会被告知或被告知计算机科学是针对特定类型的人的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's really sad to hear that it's heading in the wrong direction. What do you think is contributing to that?
turns.zh: 听说它正朝着错误的方向前进，真是令人难过。您认为是什么促成了这一点？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: I think there is still a lot of this mental model of what a computer scientist is able to do and how much support they're given. So it's been shown in studies that at the youngest generation middle school, high school, you are more likely to be given introductory STEM classes as a male than as a female. So women just aren't targeted for STEM at that younger age. And so when they enter the high school or college classes for computer science, they're way behind. And that does not feel good. No one likes to be the worst in the class. And so it's more likely that you'll drop out. We've seen studies at Carnegie Mellon that actually would create introductory computer science classes before the college class starts. And for the women who did join those classes, they actually graduated at similar rates as their male counterparts. So it's really setting them up for success.
turns.zh: 我认为仍然存在很多关于计算机科学家能够做什么以及他们获得多少支持的心理模型。研究表明，在最年轻的一代初中、高中，男性比女性更有可能接受 STEM 入门课程。因此，女性在那么年轻的时候并不是 STEM 的目标。因此，当他们进入高中或大学计算机科学课程时，他们就远远落后了。这感觉不太好。没有人喜欢成为班上最差的。所以你更有可能辍学。我们已经看到卡内基梅隆大学的研究实际上会在大学课程开始之前开设计算机科学入门课程。对于参加这些课程的女性来说，她们的毕业率实际上与男性同行相似。所以这确实为他们的成功奠定了基础。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: If folks want to help. You said that there's a PayPal page. Is there any other sort of action people can take?
turns.zh: 如果人们愿意帮忙的话。你说有一个 PayPal 页面。人们还可以采取其他行动吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yes. Enterprise software. We love to teach iOS development, licensed software. We have hundreds of students a year, so let us know.
turns.zh: 是的。企业软件。我们喜欢教授 iOS 开发、许可软件。我们每年有数百名学生，所以请告诉我们。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. And they can reach you on generationgirl.com?
turns.zh: 惊人的。他们可以通过 Generationgirl.com 联系到您吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Generationgirl.org.
turns.zh: Generationgirl.org。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Crystal, thank you so much for being here. I've taken enough of your time. Two last quick questions. Where can folks find you online if they want to reach out? And then other than the Generation Girl chat we just had, is there any other way folks can be helpful to you?
turns.zh: 水晶，非常感谢你来到这里。我已经占用你足够多的时间了。最后两个问题。如果人们想联系您，可以在哪里找到您？那么除了我们刚刚进行的“Generation Girl”聊天之外，人们还有其他方式可以帮助您吗？

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Yes. Please find me at crystalwidjaja.com. You can reach out to me and my email is there. Listeners, please do instrumentation correctly. Please don't track your KPIs. Please track your user journeys and experiences. We'll have much funner things to talk about if you do that.
turns.zh: 是的。请在 crystalwidjaja.com 上找到我。您可以联系我，我的电子邮件就在那里。各位听众，请正确地演奏乐器。请不要跟踪您的 KPI。请跟踪您的用户旅程和体验。如果你这样做的话，我们会有很多有趣的事情可以谈论。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing PSA. Thank you so much, Crystal.
turns.zh: 惊人的公益广告。非常感谢你，水晶。

turns.speaker: Crystal Widjaja
turns.en: Thanks Lenny. This was a blast.
turns.zh: 谢谢莱尼。这真是太棒了。

turns.en: Thank you so much for listening.
